doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

title: Singers with the band and the Mosaic live recordings
summary: The band loved Sinatra, Eckstine, Vaughan and Bennett for their jazz mentality; the 1959-62 live recordings are documented in a Mosaic set.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Eleven years, wow. And you had mentioned Sinatra, and thinking about vocalists, did the guys in the band ever kind of resent the vocalist being out front and doing four or five songs a night and was that something that you guys felt like you didn’t feel it was necessary?

Well the professionalism in this particular orchestra didn’t allow for that kind of attitude on a large scale. And we loved Sinatra, we loved Billy Eckstine, we loved Sarah Vaughan and we loved Tony Bennett, and there just was no feeling of that kind. Whenever we knew we were going to work with them we said well we’re going to have some fun now. Some others, who shall remain nameless, we didn’t have as much fun with because some of them didn’t have the quality arrangements that we would like to play, and some of them didn’t have that jazz singer mentality. Now see the Sinatras, the Joe Williams, Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald, Tony Bennett, they have jazz singer mentalities. In other words, you sing a chorus, somebody stands up and blows a chorus. Somebody else stands up and blows a chorus, then you come back and sing a chorus. Some singers who just have a pop singer mentality. Give me an introduction, I sing my song, nobody solos, and I take it out, and everybody is happy, or at least I’m happy. So any singers/vocalists with a jazz singer mentality we accepted. Those with the pop singer mentality we rejected.
Well you certainly had a powerhouse band there for those years, plus with Joe Williams on board, and a great time. Fortunately you recorded a lot so it’s documented.
Yes. It definitely is documented, especially in the Mosaic series of live recordings between 1959 and ‘62. That is Count Basie, the New Testament Count Basie.
